label: input token e during the original phase
explanation: Single-token detector: fires on every original-phase step whose input is the letter e (dev precision 1.00, recall 0.97, F1 0.99) and on essentially nothing else; it does not fire on other letters, digits, or <DEL>. In the copy phase, when the model feeds e back in as its own output, the feature mostly stays silent; the remaining 0.8% of mass comes from weak (~0.2 of max) activations on the copied e at recall_idx 1, i.e. when the sequence began with e. Magnitude: an isolated e gives roughly 0.55-0.72 of max. An e that directly follows another e in the original sequence is higher (about 0.9-1.0 of max), which gives the top activations, e.g. e e e. These magnitude notes come from examples only.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test score: precision 1.000, recall 0.973, F1 0.986, mass recall 0.992. There is only 1 false positive in the test set (an e in the original phase that stays inactive).

All 2988 missed test activations are weak (about 0.2 of max) copy-phase e inputs at recall_idx 1, i.e. the copied orig(0)=e. This matches the explanation. Adding these to the predicate gives F1 0.940 because the copied e at recall_idx 1 fires only 17% of the time (precision 0.17), so the original predicate is the better one.

Magnitude claims hold up in direction. An e directly after another e falls mostly in the top activation quartile (coverage by quartile, lowest to highest: 0.004 / 0.010 / 0.013 / 0.082). An e at t=0 sits only in the upper half. The exact 0.55-0.72 and 0.9-1.0 ranges were not checked, and the explanation itself says they come from examples only.
Minor overclaim: the explanation says the feature does not fire on other letters or <DEL>. It actually has 33 activations on f and 5 on <DEL> in the dev split. That is negligible noise.
